intro: Francistown is Botswana's second city, in the north-east of the country near the border with Zimbabwe. About eleven kilometres north of it, on the bank of a sandy riverbed, a reader photographed a monkey thorn, Senegalia galpinii, that towers over the bush around it. They put its trunk at about 450 centimetres round. We have no age for it yet, and would like to know what the people who live along this river call it.

trees.story:
"Senegalia galpinii," wrote the reader who sent us this tree from a sandy riverbed about eleven kilometres north of Francistown in Botswana, with a GPS fix taken below it. Its common name is the monkey thorn, a southern African cousin of the acacias, and this one stands far above everything around it.

The photograph makes the scale plain. Two people wade barefoot through a thin sheet of water on the sand, and behind them the bank rises in a dense green wall of bush. Out of that wall climbs a single bare trunk, which forks into a few great limbs and then opens into a wide, flat crown of feathery leaves against a hard blue sky. The people barely reach the foot of the bush beneath it.

The reader puts its trunk at about 450 centimetres round. That is their figure, not one we have seen measured, and we have no age for the tree. If you know this stretch of river, what the people living near it call the tree, or how old it might be, tell us here and we will add it.

Stand out on the open sand, where the reader stood, to take in the whole crown at once.
